sovereign_country.strategic_role: 连接拉美市场的欧洲商贸桥梁、本地化仓配与数字游民签证

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Procurement of Culinary and Ceremonial Grade Matcha

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-United Kingdom Trade and Cooperation Agreement (2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (as amended by Ley 7/2021); Ley 5/2015, de 27 de abril, de la obligación de información sobre los beneficiarios finales de las personas jurídicas.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Equivalent from Home Country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority in country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against UN, EU, Spanish, and OFAC PEP and sanctions lists using automated compliance tools compliant with AMLD5/6 standards.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish language and Latin alphabet; no transliteration required for standard names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, file administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) to the Registro Mercantil within one month; further judicial review available if necessary.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for SL entities provided registered office is properly documented and address is verifiable; no physical presence required but must comply with tax substance rules if applicable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (under 5% for standard SL incorporations without red flags)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for SL formation (approximately 600-1000 EUR)
Fixed fees per Registro Mercantil tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Hague Apostille Authority or Consular Office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for AML due diligence
Statutory tariff or prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 19-24, 28-30, 33-35, 62, 78-79, 159-208, 209-251, and 285-290; Law 14/2013 on support for entrepreneurs and internationalization for CIRCE and standardized formations; Regulation of the Mercantile Registry approved by Royal Decree 1784/1996.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the province where the company has its registered office, coordinated electronically through the Central Mercantile Registry and the CIRCE system administered by the Directorate General of Industry and Small and Medium Enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) containing the articles of association and subscriber details, followed by registration with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum capital of an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1.00. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. No mandatory escrow account exists; a bank certificate of deposit may be used, although the founders may assume joint liability for the accuracy of the contribution declaration where legally permitted. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and, upon liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and actual capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board acknowledges the duly executed incorporation deed and resolves to accept and record the subscription and full payment of the issued shares by the founding shareholder in accordance with the articles. The Board adopts the registered office stated in the deed as the company’s official domicile and authorizes its filing with the Mercantile Registry and tax authorities. The Board appoints [Name] as sole director, or confirms the directors named in the deed, with authority to open bank accounts, obtain tax and electronic identification credentials, execute ordinary commercial contracts, and complete all post-incorporation registrations and licenses. The secretary is authorized to certify this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), online name-certification service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names, including the intended Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada designation or SL abbreviation. Obtain the negative name certificate and ensure the exact approved name is used in the articles and public deed. The certificate is generally valid for three months for deed execution and six months for reservation purposes.
required_dossiers: Up to five proposed company names
Power of attorney if filed by an authorized representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an alternative name request or correct the objection identified by the Central Mercantile Registry. Renew the certificate if the execution period expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notarial Office selected by the founders; CIRCE/DUE platform may be used for standardized formations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles covering name, purpose, registered office, capital, share allocation, management structure, and rules for shareholder meetings. Execute the public deed before a Spanish notary. Foreign corporate shareholders must provide legalized or apostilled incorporation documents, current good-standing evidence, beneficial-owner information, and sworn Spanish translations where required.
required_dossiers: Founders’ passports or national identity documents
Foreigner Identification Numbers (NIE) for non-Spanish founders and directors
Evidence of capital contribution or founders’ contribution declaration
Foreign corporate documents with apostille or legalization and Spanish translation, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure notarial observations before execution. If a foreign document is defective, obtain a replacement, apostille or legalization, and sworn translation before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT), Form 036 or CIRCE/DUE electronic channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 with the executed deed or authorized draft documentation to obtain the company’s provisional Spanish tax identification number (NIF). Select the appropriate business activity, tax domicile, VAT status, and electronic-notification address. Register the beneficial-owner and representative information requested by the AEAT.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond electronically or through the relevant AEAT office to any identity, domicile, representation, or beneficial-ownership query. Correct Form 036 and refile supporting documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Mercantile Registry of the province of the registered office; electronic submission may be arranged by the notary or CIRCE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized incorporation deed, articles, provisional NIF, and any required beneficial-ownership information. Pay the applicable Mercantile Registry tariff and monitor the registry entry. Registration gives the company full legal personality as an SL and permits issuance of the definitive NIF after tax notification.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership declaration or registry information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a suspension or defect notice, obtain the official defect note, cure each defect through the notary or authorized filer, and resubmit within the applicable statutory period. Appeal to the Directorate General of Legal Security and Public Faith where appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Definitive NIF and Complete Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT electronic office or competent AEAT office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notify the AEAT of Mercantile Registry registration using Form 036 and obtain the definitive NIF. Confirm the economic activity classification, VAT registration, intra-Community VAT registration where EU trade is anticipated, and electronic notification address. Register for the EU VIES system before making qualifying intra-Community supplies or acquisitions.
required_dossiers: Mercantile Registry certificate or registration details
Digital certificate or authorized electronic representative evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct activity codes, VAT selections, or representative information and submit a replacement Form 036. Resolve AEAT verification requests before commencing invoicing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Governance Records and Operational Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company’s registered-office notary, Mercantile Registry, relevant Autonomous Community authority, and municipal authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt and sign the first board or sole-director resolution, open the corporate bank account, maintain the share register and minutes book, legalize corporate books electronically through the Mercantile Registry, and register the beneficial-owner record when required. For packaged matcha distribution, notify or register the food business with the competent Autonomous Community authority and verify municipal activity, premises, signage, waste, and warehouse requirements.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or sole-director decision
Food business notification or registration filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to regional or municipal requests for premises plans, food-safety procedures, storage details, or waste documentation. Amend the filing or obtain the required municipal declaration, license, or inspection clearance before operating the affected premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent food-control and industrial authority of the Autonomous Community where the warehouse or establishment is located, together with the relevant municipal authority. For a pure distributor of sealed, pre-packed matcha, the applicable requirement is ordinarily a food-business notification or registration rather than a manufacturing license. If the company imports from outside the European Union, customs, food-import, and border-control registrations also apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Registration or Prior Notification (Registro Sanitario de Empresas y Productos Alimentarios or applicable Autonomous Community food-business notification); municipal activity or opening authorization for the warehouse, where required. No general manufacturing operating permit applies to simple wholesale distribution of sealed products.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community, applying Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment and, where nationally competent, the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally Exempt from formal EIA for ordinary storage and wholesale distribution without manufacturing, significant emissions, or hazardous processes. A warehouse may nevertheless require municipal environmental communication, waste registration, or an integrated environmental authorization if its scale, installations, refrigeration systems, fuel use, or waste profile triggers regional rules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable municipal or Autonomous Community wastewater discharge limits; do not discharge process effluent without authorization. Maintain refrigerants and combustion equipment under applicable fluorinated-gas and air-quality rules. Control dust and VOC emissions where generated, segregate food and packaging waste, use authorized waste carriers and managers, and retain transfer records. Hazardous waste, if any, requires identification, storage, labeling, and traceability under Spanish waste legislation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal confirmation of premises compatibility, activity or opening authorization where applicable, fire-prevention compliance under the Building Technical Code and the Fire Safety Regulation for Industrial Establishments where applicable, and certified emergency systems. Verify structural floor loading, storage-rack anchoring, escape routes, emergency lighting, extinguishers, electrical installations, and warehouse fire compartmentation. Implement occupational risk prevention under Law 31/1995, including risk assessment, worker training, safe handling procedures, and documented emergency planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — official digital portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; corporate/NIF registration desk: Oficina Nacional de Recaudación (ONR); customs authority: AEAT Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Spanish SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) obtains a provisional CIF/NIF at notarial deed execution, then submits form 036 (censal de alta) to the AEAT Oficina Nacional de Recaudación within one month of incorporation to receive the definitive statutory NIF. Non-resident shareholders must appoint a fiscal representative (representante fiscal) domiciled in Spain for tax, VAT, e-invoicing and customs correspondence. Intra-EU suppliers may activate an operator code for VIES purposes; cross-border e-commerce sellers may register in the Spanish OSS portal; export traders that seek monthly VAT refunds must apply for REDEME registration through form 036 regardless of turnover.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SL is a Spanish resident taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (25% corporate income tax on worldwide profits, with territorial-source modifications for foreign branches) and is a separate taxable person for VAT (IVA) purposes. Spanish company law does not permit pass-through (check-the-box) classification for an SL; hybrid transparency arises only under ATAD rules where a foreign-law entity (e.g., US LLC) is classified differently by its home jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no US-style check-the-box election. Statutory elections available: (i) consolidated corporate tax group (Régimen de consolidación fiscal) for Spanish subsidiaries held at 75% or more by a Spanish parent; (ii) VAT group election (Grupo de entidades, Art. 19 Ley 37/1992) for closely linked Spanish entities; (iii) REDEME monthly refund election for exporters; (iv) OSS/MOSS one-stop-shop election for intra-EU distance sales and digital services; (v) patent-box and R&D tax-credit elections; (vi) ATAD hybrid-mismatch transparency adjustments under Ley 11/2021, including formal AEAT disclosure of asymmetrical entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), governed by Ley 37/1992 and Real Decreto 1624/1992, with special regimes for REDEME, SII, Verifactu and OSS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 — no de-minimis registration threshold exists; any taxable person performing taxable supplies (including import of matcha powder) must register before the first supply. Procedural thresholds: EUR 100,000 annual turnover for quarterly VAT returns; EUR 6,000,000 annual turnover for monthly returns, SII real-time book reporting and mandatory B2B e-invoicing. Export traders should register in REDEME irrespective of turnover to claim monthly refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing (Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece') applies from 2024. The Verifactu technical standard (RD 1007/2023) requires all billing software to issue invoices with integrity hash and QR code, and to transmit invoice metadata to AEAT through the Verifactu/SII API in near real time. Large taxpayers and REDEME-registered exporters must file VAT books electronically within 4 calendar days of each reporting period through SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información). Digital stamping is not used for fiscal clearance; customs clearance operates through the DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) and the Export Control System (ECS).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Art. 21 Ley 37/1992, exports of goods to third countries are zero-rated (0% IVA) provided the goods physically leave EU customs territory: the exporter must (i) hold a valid customs export declaration DUA and MRN; (ii) complete exportation within 60 days of the taxable supply; (iii) prove physical departure through transport documents (Bill of Lading or Air Waybill) within the statutory period; and (iv) retain complete records for 4 years. Intra-EU dispatches are exempt through VIES when the customer provides a valid Spanish/EU VAT ID. Organic matcha powder qualifies for zero-rating only where the goods are genuinely exported without transformation, re-entry, or partial consumption during transport. Input VAT on procurement, packaging, warehousing and freight is recoverable through REDEME monthly refund returns.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DUA) and corresponding MRN issued by AEAT customs office or authorised customs agent; Exit Summary Declaration where required
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical departure from EU customs territory
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the Spanish SL as exporter and the consignee outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT TT receipt evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Certificates of origin, EUR.1 or EUR-MED movement certificate, phytosanitary certificates and organic matcha certificates required by destination-country customs
REDEME registration status confirmation and export records retained for 4 years under Art. 24 Ley 37/1992
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audits export zero-rating through ex-post desk reviews, end-of-year export registers, and cross-checks against customs ECS data, port movement records, Bills of Lading and bank SWIFT records. Absent valid physical export or complete documentary proof, the zero rate is clawed back at 21% with late-payment interest (currently 5% per annum), plus tax penalties: minor documentary irregularities 50%–100% of the tax due; intentional evasion 100%–150% of the tax due. Fraudulent refund claims exceeding EUR 120,000 trigger criminal prosecution under Art. 305 Código Penal (2–6 years imprisonment and a fine of 2–6 times the tax evaded), with the tax debt suspended pending judgment, civil recovery, loss of REDEME status and disqualification from public benefits and subsidies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; applicable foreign-exchange rules also derive from European Union payment-services, sanctions, anti-money-laundering, and capital-movement legislation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and has full current-account and capital-account convertibility within the European Union framework. A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may receive foreign investment, pay suppliers abroad, repatriate dividends, repay shareholder loans, and remit liquidation proceeds without a general exchange-control approval or mandatory conversion into euros. Banks may require evidence of the commercial purpose, beneficial ownership, source of funds, tax status, sanctions screening, and corporate authorization. Dividend distributions must comply with Spanish company-law requirements, including distributable-profit, net-asset, statutory-reserve, and solvency limitations. Dividend withholding tax may apply, subject to domestic exemptions, applicable tax treaties, and European Union parent-subsidiary relief. Payments involving sanctioned jurisdictions, restricted counterparties, dual-use goods, or suspicious trade documentation may be blocked or reported.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement for exporters to surrender export proceeds to the central bank, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general fixed deadline for converting foreign-currency export receipts. The company may retain foreign-currency balances or convert receipts at commercially agreed rates, subject to bank controls and accounting in euros. Export transactions must be supported by invoices, contracts, transport or customs evidence where applicable, and payment records. Cross-border payment and foreign-asset reporting may be required under Banco de España statistical reporting rules, including periodic reporting applicable to residents with material cross-border transactions or foreign financial assets. Cash entering or leaving the European Union with EUR 10,000 or more, or its equivalent, is subject to customs declaration requirements. Banks remain subject to Spanish and EU anti-money-laundering, sanctions, and transaction-monitoring duties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection, SEPA transfers, multi-currency accounts, supplier payments, and foreign-exchange execution where the provider is an EU-authorized electronic money institution or payment institution operating in Spain through valid passporting or Spanish authorization. An electronic money institution is not a deposit-taking bank and generally cannot provide ordinary bank deposits, unrestricted credit, or a statutory capital escrow function. Customer funds must be safeguarded rather than treated as bank deposits. The provider may impose country, industry, transaction-volume, virtual-asset, high-risk-jurisdiction, or correspondent-banking restrictions. The Spanish SL should maintain a regulated Spanish or EU bank account for tax payments, payroll, capital contributions, emergency liquidity, and critical supplier continuity. Offshore digital EMIs without EU authorization, valid passporting, or adequate safeguarding should not be used for core treasury operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not universally require directors to attend a bank branch physically. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified electronic identification, video identification, electronic certificates, or other bank-approved methods. In practice, banks may require an in-person meeting, live video interview, certified identification, Spanish tax identification numbers, notarized or apostilled foreign documents, or verification of the Spanish registered office. At least one authorized signatory, the ultimate beneficial owners, and controlling persons must be identified. Non-resident directors or shareholders commonly face enhanced verification and may need to provide proof of address, tax residence, source of wealth, and evidence of a genuine Spanish operating nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner with incomplete Spanish or foreign identification data.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current registry extract; notarized articles of association; shareholder register; ownership chart to natural-person beneficial owners; passports or national identity documents; proof of residential address; Spanish tax identification numbers where required; director appointment evidence; powers of attorney; and certified translations, apostilles, or legalization where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership, nominee ownership, layered holding companies, or unexplained control rights.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed ownership and control chart; constitutional documents for every intermediate entity; shareholder registers; ultimate-beneficial-owner declarations; board resolutions; trust or nominee disclosures where applicable; evidence of voting rights; and written explanations of the commercial rationale for the ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Matcha imports involving Asian suppliers, intermediary companies, unusual jurisdictions, or payment routes inconsistent with the supplier contract.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier master file; executed purchase contracts; commercial invoices; purchase orders; bills of lading or airway bills; customs declarations; certificates of origin; organic certification and food-compliance documents where applicable; shipping and insurance records; supplier ownership information; sanctions screening; and a transaction-flow memorandum linking each payment to the underlying shipment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or rapidly increasing transaction volumes inconsistent with the company's financial statements, business plan, or stated low-risk profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved business plan; 12-month cash-flow forecast; customer contracts; purchase and sales ledgers; VAT and corporate tax filings; management accounts; inventory records; warehouse or logistics agreements; financing documents; audited or accountant-prepared financial statements; and an explanation of seasonal procurement and working-capital cycles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound shareholder funding described only as a generic transfer or received from an account not held by the shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital-increase or shareholder-loan agreement; shareholder and board resolutions; bank statements showing the remitter; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; notarial and Commercial Registry filings where applicable; beneficial-owner confirmation; tax analysis; and a written payment-purpose instruction stating equity contribution, shareholder loan, or other legally accurate purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned countries, sanctioned persons, restricted banks, dual-use goods, or adverse media.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty screening results; supplier and customer due-diligence files; sanctions representations; end-use and end-user statements; product classification; customs and transport documents; independent adverse-media review; compliance officer approval; and documented escalation to the bank before execution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Organic-product claims, food-safety concerns, or discrepancies between product descriptions, customs codes, invoices, and payment instructions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid organic certification; certificates of analysis; food-business registrations where applicable; product specifications; batch and traceability records; customs classification memorandum; import documentation; laboratory reports; insurance documents; and written reconciliation of product, quantity, price, currency, and beneficiary data.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, cash-intensive settlement, third-party payment providers, or unexplained payment splitting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy; approved bank-account matrix; segregation-of-duties controls; payment approval logs; counterparty bank-account verification; written explanation of any third-party payment; beneficial-owner confirmations; invoices and settlement reconciliations; and a commitment to route corporate transactions through accounts held in the company's name.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity contributions through a regulated Spanish or EU bank account in the exact legal name of the Spanish SL. Before transfer, provide the bank with the capital-increase or shareholder-loan documentation, shareholder resolution, source-of-funds evidence, beneficial-owner information, remitting-account details, and expected amount and currency. Use the bank's accurate payment-purpose classification; Spain does not impose a single universal central-bank purpose-code system for ordinary corporate wires, so the bank's internal purpose categories and applicable ISO 20022 or SWIFT data should be used without misclassification. Equity contributions should be reconciled to the notarial and Commercial Registry process where a formal capital increase is implemented. Shareholder loans should be documented separately and should state principal, maturity, interest, repayment terms, transfer-pricing support where relevant, and lender identity. Retain MT103 or equivalent payment confirmation, bank credit advice, accounting entries, and supporting corporate approvals. Avoid third-party remitters, cash deposits, payment splitting, and transfers from unrelated jurisdictions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments to eligible SEPA beneficiaries and SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly evidenced by an MT103 or ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. Each payment should identify the beneficiary's legal name, account or IBAN, BIC where applicable, invoice number, purchase-order reference, goods description, currency, amount, and contractual payment terms. For higher-value, new-counterparty, or document-sensitive purchases, use a commercial documentary letter of credit, preferably irrevocable and subject to UCP 600, with clearly specified presentation documents, shipment terms, insurance, inspection, origin, and organic-certification requirements. Documentary collections may be used where counterparties and jurisdictions are well established. Banks may require customs, transport, invoice, sanctions, and trade-based money-laundering documentation before releasing funds. Maintain three-way reconciliation among purchase order, goods-receipt or shipping evidence, and invoice, with dual approval for beneficiary changes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/JPY, EUR/GBP, and other bank-offered forward exchange contracts for forecast supplier payments or customer receipts, subject to documented underlying exposure and bank suitability requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with limited convertibility or local-market restrictions, where offered by an appropriately regulated bank or investment firm and supported by a documented commercial exposure.
Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for recurring or longer-term funding exposures, subject to negotiated master documentation, collateral terms, valuation, and counterparty-credit limits.
FX spot transactions for ordinary conversion of trade receipts and payments.

Options or collars may be used for material exposures where the company understands premium, settlement, liquidity, and loss risks; execution should be governed by an approved derivatives policy and appropriate bank documentation.

All derivatives should be executed with regulated counterparties under appropriate ISDA or equivalent documentation, with confirmation of notional, maturity, fixing, settlement, collateral, early-termination, and close-out terms. The company should maintain hedge documentation, exposure forecasts, valuation records, accounting treatment, and EMIR or other applicable reporting assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approved annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, statement of changes in equity, notes) deposited at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the province of the registered office (Registro Mercantil; central electronic filing via the Registro Mercantil Central platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval within 6 months of the fiscal year-end; Registry deposit within 1 month of approval; for a 31-December year-end the deposit must be completed by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry folio closure (cierre registral): no corporate act, share transfer, appointment or capital change can be registered until the accounts are deposited (LSC art. 283); late or omitted deposit is fined EUR 1,200–60,000; automatic strike-off does not apply to an active SL, but the closure blocks all subsequent registrations and distributions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization / stamping of official corporate and accounting books (Register of Members, Minute Book, inventory and annual accounts book, daily journal, invoice register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the province of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounting books must be presented for legalization within 4 months after each fiscal year-end (by 30 April for a calendar-year company); corporate register books are legalized before first use or together with the annual presentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-legalized books are not admissible as evidence in favour of the company in commercial proceedings (C.Com. art. 326); administrative fines under C.Com. arts. 200–201 and loss of evidentiary value in shareholder or creditor disputes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return — Modelo 200 (with balance sheet reconciliation, tax adjustments and credit claims)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the conclusion of the 6-month period following the tax year-end; for a 31-December year-end the filing window is 1–25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 20% if filed within 12 months after the deadline, 35% if filed later (LGT art. 27); 150% surcharge plus fixed penalties up to EUR 2,000 for non-filing; default interest accrues from the day after the deadline

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 January following the close of the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission penalty of EUR 150–600 under LGT art. 199; late-filing surcharges of 20%/35% on any VAT balance due plus default interest

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of ultimate beneficial owners in the Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro de Titularidades Reales, RTR), filed together with the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the registered office (RTR module administered by the Registrars)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO data must be current as at the date of the annual accounts deposit (by 31 July for a calendar-year company); any shareholding transfer of 25% or more, or any change of effective control, must be declared within 10 days of the corporate resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Obsolete RTR data blocks registration of subsequent corporate acts and share transfers; breach of the UBO reporting duty is a serious AML infringement under Law 10/2010 with fines up to EUR 100,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Related-party transactions and foreign-holding information return — Modelo 232 (applicable only if related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000, or the company holds a 50% or greater interest in a foreign entity, or specific board and reporting thresholds are met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed within the corporate income tax window, 1–25 July for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: EUR 200 penalty per omitted or incorrect data record (LGT art. 199); corrected returns filed within 6 months reduce the penalty to 75% of the base; failure to file attracts the same surcharges as Modelo 200

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is mandatory when the SL meets at least two of the three tests for two consecutive years: total assets above EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover above EUR 5,700,000; average headcount above 50 (LSC art. 263). An organic matcha powder trading SL below these thresholds has no compulsory audit; if voluntary audit is commissioned, the auditor's report must still be deposited together with the annual accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP — Plan General de Contabilidad (RD 1514/2007, as updated by RD 1/2021); the PGC de PYMES and the simplified PGC micro-enterprise variant are available to companies not exceeding, for two consecutive years, two of these limits: assets EUR 2,850,000, net turnover EUR 5,700,000, 50 employees; IFRS-EU is not required for a private unaudited SL importing and distributing culinary and ceremonial matcha powder.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not require a standalone annual UBO filing: the RTR record is confirmed and updated at the moment the annual accounts are deposited, and the Registrar verifies that the beneficial-ownership data is consistent with the Register of Members. Each transfer of 25% or more of the share capital, or any change of effective control, must be reported to the RTR using the official form within 10 days of the corporate resolution; the Register of Members must simultaneously be updated for every share transfer, and the year-end legalization of that register evidences the ownership chain. For a calendar-year SL the annual UBO confirmation is fully satisfied no later than 31 July together with the accounts deposit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors appointments as evidenced in the public Commercial Registry file
Register of Contracts with the Sole Shareholder (Libro de Contratos del Socio Único) when the SL has a single member
Accounting books: Inventory and Annual Accounts book, Daily Journal, invoice register

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $650–$2,400 (Spanish gestoría/asesoría or registered-agent equivalent covering seat address, statutory-book legalization workflow, registry filings and the annual compliance calendar)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $0 when the statutory audit thresholds are not met; EUR 2,500–EUR 8,000 (about $2,700–$8,700) if an audit is triggered by growth or voluntarily commissioned by shareholders

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly incorporated SLs in the first two tax periods with positive taxable base, provided the company engages in an economic activity; statutory deductions for R&D, job creation for disabled persons, and certain film expenditures; no matcha-specific tax holiday exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 – Impuesto sobre Sociedades, submitted electronically via the AEAT Sede Electrónica (Spanish Tax Agency online portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual CIT return; quarterly advance payments (Modelo 202 or 222) are also required during the tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the expiry of six months after the tax period end; calendar-year entities file between 1 and 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: NIF (tax ID), corporate name, registered office and tax domicile.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Filed by the Spanish SL; foreign shareholders should ensure the SL's NIF is valid and the corporate address is current for treaty application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result: profit or loss per audited annual accounts before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent companies must verify that intercompany margins are at arm's length, as corrections affect dividend WHT and transfer-pricing exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Negative tax base offset: application of prior-year tax losses to the current positive taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Owners may require loss-offset forecasts; losses expire after 10 years and are not automatically transferred abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholdings and payments on account: taxes withheld by third parties (rental income, interest, professional fees) creditable against CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not directly applicable to non-resident shareholders; any domestic WHT on Spanish-source income is credited against Spanish CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax settlement: taxable base, tax rate, deductions, full tax payable, credits, and resulting debt or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The settled taxable profit is the distributable base; subsequent dividend distributions to foreign shareholders trigger Spanish WHT at 19%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a late-payment surcharge (recargo) of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (3-6 months), 15% (6-12 months), or 20% (>12 months) plus late-payment interest; a minimum penalty of EUR 200 applies if the final tax due is nil. Underdeclaration penalties range from 50% to 75% of the omitted amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% (general non-resident rate; 24% for non-cooperative jurisdictions without DTA; treaty rates may reduce to 0%-15%)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, file with the Spanish SL the foreign Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) and a beneficial ownership declaration before the dividend payment date to apply the reduced rate at source. For EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, verify participation thresholds (≥5% or ≥10%) and required holding period; if excess WHT was withheld, file Modelo 210 with the AEAT within four years to claim a refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: domestic statutory 19% for EU/EEA and DTA partners, 24% for non-cooperative third states; DTA rates typically 0%-10%. Royalties: domestic statutory 24%; DTA rates typically 5%-10%; an exemption from WHT on interest and royalties may apply under EU Directive 2003/49/EC for associated EU companies with economic substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 45,000,000 annual net turnover triggers mandatory Master File and Local File; for entities below this threshold, related-party transactions exceeding EUR 250,000 per transaction category in a tax period require simplified contemporaneous documentation (administrative guidance and supporting records).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, EU ATAD anti-abuse rules, the Spanish GAAR (Article 15 LGT) and judicial anti-fraud doctrine require the Spanish SL to maintain real personnel, premises and operational activity so as to be the beneficial owner of income and to obtain DTA or EU directive relief. A hollow or 'letterbox' entity may be disregarded, with income recharacterized and penalties imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating income or inflating deductible costs (e.g., fake procurement invoices for matcha) so that the amount evaded exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code Article 305: imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to 6 times the defrauded amount; loss of tax benefits, subsidies and public contracts for up to 5 years; the company itself faces penalties under Articles 310 bis and 327, including fines of 2 to 6 times the amount and potential winding-up.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ordered or facilitated evasion are jointly and severally liable for tax debts under Article 42 LGT (piercing the corporate veil); criminal conviction may be accompanied by restitution orders, travel bans, and disqualification from commercial management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a nominal distribution entity without real substance (no employees, no office, no business decision-making) solely to channel matcha trading profits and obtain treaty benefits or EU directive exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR under Article 15 LGT and ATAD rules: the arrangement is disregarded, income is recharacterized at the beneficial owner level, treaty rights denied, CIT recalculated, and a penalty equal to 25% of the avoided tax (or 50% if an abusive tax scheme) is imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally implicated in the sham; the corporate veil is pierced and liabilities are imposed on directors for corporate debts, fines and criminal elements; travel bans and imprisonment may follow if the tax amount exceeds EUR 120,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the matcha distribution entity as a pass-through for illicit funds (e.g., structuring Swift TT and wire transfers from unrelated parties under false matcha invoices).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish AML Law (Ley 10/2010) imposes administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 or six times the value of the funds; Criminal Code Article 301 imposes imprisonment of 3 to 6 years and a fine of up to three times the laundered amount; the company may be disqualified or dissolved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors deliberately involved are criminally liable and subject to personal fines, asset seizure, travel bans and imprisonment; they may also be banned from holding directorship roles in Spain.
